B. Is this measure already running in Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure lead to lung cancer being found at an earlier stage, and by how much?
Measure: Symptom awareness campaign (cough over three weeks). A campaign on the English "Be Clear on Cancer" model telling people with a persistent cough to see a doctor. Weak evidence: in England the share found at stage I rose during the campaign months and faded within months, so it has to be repeated every year, and the extra GP visits and chest X-rays cost several times the advertising.
effect_summary_en: England's national cough campaign raised the share of NSCLC found at stage I by 3.1 percentage points during the campaign; how long the effect lasted is not shown in what I read.
supported_en: British Journal of Cancer (2015): during England's national campaign, the share of NSCLC found at stage I rose 3.1 points and resections rose 2.3 points.
not_supported_en: The passages I read do not show how long the effect lasted, so the 0.8-point yearly average is not confirmed. The MSD campaign has no published effect in Finland.
in_use_summary_en: MSD's nationwide "Hakeudu hoitoon" lung symptom campaign has run every year since 2020 in November–December. Kymenhva's and HUS's pages show no campaign of their own.
summary_en: Neither Kymenhva's lung cancer page nor HUS's lung cancer care-pathway page shows its own campaign telling people with a cough lasting over three weeks to see a doctor. However, the drug company MSD says its nationwide "Hakeudu hoitoon" campaign has urged people with lung symptoms to see a doctor every November–December since 2020. The 2015 British Journal of Cancer evaluation of England's national campaign found a 3.1 percentage point rise in stage I NSCLC during the campaign and a 63% rise in GP visits for cough, but the passages I read do not show how long this lasted. Check: The page quoted for use does not name Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county or its university hospital area near the quote, so local use is reported as no public sign of it.
unanswered_en: I found no Kymenhva or HUS decision on a cough campaign, and the passages I read do not say how long the English stage shift lasted.
